subject: Biotechnology
title: Gene Editing in Human Embryos
description: A quick, practical guide to Gene Editing in Human Embryos.

hook.text: In 2018, He Jiankui edited twin human embryos with CRISPR — the world was shocked, not impressed.

buildup.text: He claimed to disable CCR5, an HIV co-receptor — intending to make the babies resistant to HIV infection.

discovery.text: The edits were incomplete and introduced unintended mutations — mosaicism meant not all cells carried the change.

twist.text: CCR5 deletion may increase susceptibility to West Nile virus — the supposed benefit came with unknown risks.

climax.text: He was sentenced to three years in prison — the scientific community declared a moratorium on heritable editing.

punchline.text: He edited humans before science was ready — ethics cannot be optional.

quiz.question: Why was He Jiankui's experiment widely condemned?
options: The CRISPR technology he used was outdated
He edited human embryos without proper safety data, consent processes, or scientific justification
The babies did not survive the editing procedure
